task: Phase 5 Step 2 -- LinkedIn offline integration design/specification only, no implementation
based_solely_on: existing, unmodified adapter architecture (source_adapter.py, source_registry.py, discover_local.py, canonical_job.py, cross_source_dedup.py, job_id.py, location_taxonomy.py, freshness.py, experience_eligibility.py)

1_adapter_boundary.proposed_class: LinkedInAdapter(JobSourceAdapter) in scripts/linkedin_adapter.py -- same existing file, extended in place, no new file/class name
responsibilities_in_scope: constructing a LinkedIn-specific query for whatever the eventual official API's request shape is
making the request via an injectable fetcher object (mirrors NaukriAdapter(fetcher=...))
classifying the raw response into a small LinkedIn-specific state set, raising AdapterBlockedError/AdapterTimeoutError
mapping the response into the existing flat raw-job dict shape
declaring status/capabilities truthfully, only once demonstrated

SEARCH.classification: potentially available through an official API
SEARCH.basis: guest search page returns real results but access path is unauthorized; official API search functionality presumed but not confirmed

DETAIL.basis: 61 detail links observed, none visited (Phase 5 Step 1)

NATIVE_FRESHNESS.basis: a freshness URL parameter is commonly rumored for LinkedIn's consumer search but was not verified live in Step 1

PAGINATION.basis: implied by result-count vs. links-shown mismatch, mechanism not determined

APPLICATION_URL.classification: not applicable to guest access; unknown for an official API
APPLICATION_URL.basis: robots.txt explicitly disallows /jobs/view/externalApply/ and /job-apply/ even for named, permitted bots

COMPANY_METADATA.basis: not confirmed extractable even from the one guest page visited

REMOTE_FILTER.basis: not tested at all in Step 1

LOCATION_FILTER.basis: the one guest page visited did honor a location value in its URL/title; not confirmed for an official API or as a structured filter vs. keyword matching

3_search_input_mapping.role: would map to the official API's keyword/title-query parameter -- no parameter name proposed, none observed
3_search_input_mapping.location: would map to the official API's location parameter -- plausible free-text or geo-ID basis per Step 1, official API shape unknown
3_search_input_mapping.experience_years: LinkedIn's UI is known to use bucketed experience levels (entry/associate/mid-senior/director/executive) rather than raw years -- presumed only, not verified, would need an explicit bucket mapping
3_search_input_mapping.exclude_keywords: no LinkedIn-side mechanism observed or presumed; would remain a client-side post-fetch filter
3_search_input_mapping.max_job_age_days: would map to a native freshness parameter only if NATIVE_FRESHNESS is confirmed (currently unknown); otherwise silently unsupported, matching the existing None-means-unrestricted fallback discipline
3_search_input_mapping.extra: reserved escape hatch, same pattern as naukri_adapter.py's extra['naukri_search_url']
3_search_input_mapping.pagination_as_search_input: not a SearchQuery field today for any adapter; would require a new field or per-adapter internal loop -- a real, deferred design decision
